sources: catalog/go/releases.json and catalog/go/gaps.json (for the list of majors and the go1.0/go1.1/go1.2 gap)

milestones.notes: Transparent client AND server support for HTTP/2 in net/http over HTTPS; no protocol-specific exported API. Disable via Transport.TLSNextProto / Server.TLSNextProto set to an empty map.
golang.org/x/net/context promoted into the standard library as context; adopted by net, net/http, os/exec. (Not one of SCHEMA.md's listed ids -- added because the task specifically tracks it.)
linux/arm64 shipped mostly complete but cgo only worked with external linking until later releases filled it out.

Experimental in 1.11 (GO111MODULE=auto/on/off). The auto heuristic broadened and the module proxy/checksum database became the default fetch path in 1.13. Module-aware mode became the unconditional default -- retiring GOPATH mode for ordinary builds -- in 1.16.
Opt-in via GODEBUG=tls13=1 in 1.12; enabled by default in 1.13 (opt-out via tls13=0 removed in 1.14).
fmt.Errorf's %w verb plus errors.Unwrap/Is/As. (Custom id -- not in SCHEMA.md's list.)
//go:embed directive and the embed package for compiling static files into the binary. (Custom id.)
Apple Silicon: darwin/arm64, full cgo/pie/race support from introduction.
windows/arm64, with cgo support from introduction.
Type parameters per the Type Parameters Proposal; the Go team explicitly flagged the implementation as new and not yet proven in production at release.

GOMAXPROCS now defaults to the number of available CPUs instead of 1 -- before 1.5, goroutines were concurrent but ran on a single OS thread by default even on a multi-core machine, unless the program raised GOMAXPROCS itself.
Goroutines have always been multiplexed onto OS threads by the runtime's M:N scheduler; general Go knowledge, not tied to a specific fetched release note.
windows/amd64 was supported from Go's original public release; the exact introducing version predates the go.dev/doc/go1.N release-notes archive used for this research.
go.mod/go.sum plus go get/go mod give the toolchain a real dependency resolver with version pinning; before 1.11, go get had no version resolution and everything lived flatly under GOPATH/src.
Custom id (not in SCHEMA.md's list) -- each for-loop iteration now gets its own copy of the loop variables, eliminating the classic 'goroutine captured the loop variable' bug class.
Custom id -- for-range accepts iterator functions (func(func() bool) and friends); previewed behind GOEXPERIMENT=rangefunc in 1.22, shipped as a real, non-experimental language feature in 1.23.

the go command (build, test, get, fmt, vet)
goroutines and channels
gofmt

limitations: no built-in HTTP/2 in net/http (added 1.6)
no context package in the standard library -- cancellation/deadlines/request-scoped values need golang.org/x/net/context or hand-rolled channels (added 1.7)
no module system at all -- dependencies must live under GOPATH/src with no version pinning (experimental modules added 1.11)
no TLS 1.3 support of any kind in crypto/tls (opt-in support added 1.12)
TLS 1.3 exists but is opt-in only (GODEBUG=tls13=1) -- off unless a client/server explicitly enables it (default-on from 1.13)

no error wrapping -- fmt.Errorf has no %w verb and there is no errors.Is/As/Unwrap, so building/inspecting error chains means a third-party lib (e.g. pkg/errors) or manual type assertions (added 1.13)
modules are opt-in (GO111MODULE=auto): a go.mod-less checkout under GOPATH still builds in legacy GOPATH mode (module-aware mode became the default, GOPATH mode retired, in 1.16)
no //go:embed -- bundling static assets into the binary needs a third-party generator (e.g. go-bindata) or reading files from disk at runtime (added 1.16)
no generics -- type-parameterized containers/algorithms require interface{} plus type assertions/reflection, or per-type code generation (added 1.18)

for-loop variables are created once and reused by every iteration -- capturing the loop variable in a closure or goroutine without an explicit per-iteration copy is a classic data race/bug (fixed in 1.22)
cannot range over a function -- custom iterators must be hand-written as callback-taking functions rather than used with for-range (added 1.23)
GOMAXPROCS defaults to 1 -- goroutines are concurrent but do not run in parallel on multiple cores unless the program raises GOMAXPROCS itself (default changed in 1.5)
